nodes.description: Inducible deletion of alphaENaC in the adult nephron causes hyperkalemia and weight loss on a regular-salt diet, mimicking PHA1, and a high-sodium, low-potassium diet rescues it.

Airway ENaC absorbs sodium and liquid from the airway surface. Patients with systemic PHA1 have no airway sodium absorption, more than twice the normal airway surface liquid volume, and recurrent chest congestion, cough and wheeze in early childhood. In alphaENaC-null mice airway sodium transport is abolished and neonates die from retained lung liquid, but a preterm SCNN1A-homozygous infant breathed normally after birth.

nodes.description: Biallelic SCNN1A variants remove or impair the ENaC alpha subunit. In heterologous expression the beta and gamma subunits cannot produce an amiloride-sensitive current without alpha, which may explain why SCNN1A is the gene most often affected. Missense alleles such as p.Phe226Cys reduce channel activity and expression only partly, matching their milder course.

nodes.description: In principal cells of the aldosterone-sensitive distal nephron and collecting duct, ENaC provides the rate-limiting apical step of sodium reabsorption. Without it aldosterone cannot drive sodium reabsorption, producing end-organ mineralocorticoid resistance and urinary salt wasting. Adult nephron-specific alphaENaC deletion in mice reproduces the syndrome, which no other transporter compensates except under a high-sodium, low-potassium diet.
